ops.entry: WHEN reporting a defect class closed DO run at least one probe one boundary beyond the stated class contract (adjacent configuration, caller, route or write target) and name that boundary in the claim — measuring only inside the contract leaves adjacent members for later rounds and other reviewers to find.
ops.why: Lead-relayed (ship ruling Distill): QA called stdio/journal classes closed measuring only inside the contract; reviewers found adjacent members outside it. Displaces old P-11 (whole-file grep -q), which P-02's vacuous-substring rule and G-05 already cover.

ops.entry: WHEN fail-first needs a pre-fix red and source edits are refused DO load the old blob (`git show <sha>:<path>`) into a fresh in-process module, or check the new tests into an old-SHA pin — cases spawning subprocesses re-import from disk, so only the pin reddens them.
ops.why: Own log: in-process old-blob reproduction matched the builder red except the subprocess-probe cases, which re-import the pinned module from disk; sharpens P-07 without growing it.

ops.entry: WHEN a fixture imposes hostile state for a windowed contract (e.g. post-commit stdio) DO produce it the way real callers can and apply it inside the window — state imposed earlier exercises unrelated phases whose behaviour varies by host environment, so the fixture passes locally and crashes elsewhere.
ops.why: Lead-relayed (CI fixture ruling): closing the stream object before startup passed locally but crashed CI's earlier argparse phase. Displaces G-09 (exact enum tokens), now enforced by the digest validator itself.

ops.entry: WHEN claiming a run independent of the parent session or equivalent to CI DO run every CI interpreter version and pin or diff the environment the tooling and interpreter themselves read (project-root vars, colour/TERM, buffering) — stripping one variable leaves host settings that mask failures CI will hit.
ops.why: Lead-relayed (CI fixture ruling): host NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb masked a 3.14 CI crash. Generalizes old G-11 (inherited project-root vars) into one env-parity rule, same length.

originals.original: WHEN a verify does `grep -q <literal>` against a whole file DO check where the match actually lands — the substring can be satisfied by an unrelated section, so the check gates nothing about the section it names, even though it exits 0.

WHEN fail-first needs a pre-fix red and source edits are refused DO load the old blob (`git show <sha>:<path>`) into a fresh in-process module, or check the new tests into a pin at the old SHA — either reproduces the builder's reds without touching the reviewed tree.

WHEN emitting a digest field constrained to a contract enum (e.g. severity) DO use the exact literal token the contract defines, never a synonym — a validator gating on exact string match can accept the synonym silently, and the drift then ships undetected.

WHEN running a suite in an independent clone or standalone checkout DO unset inherited project-root environment variables exported by the parent session and record the environment — tooling can resolve the parent tree, so a green or red run is not independent of it.

ops.entry: WHEN a mutant or old blob must drive test-plan-merge.py or the check-domain integration tests DO set PLAN_MERGE_BIN / CHECK_DOMAIN_BIN to a /tmp scratch tree mirroring bin/, schemas/ and .harness/team-config.yaml — those tests honour the overrides, and root resolution needs team-config.
ops.why: Own log: the overrides let mutants run under the pin's own tests without refused source edits; confirmed both env names in tests/integration (test-plan-merge.py:37, check_domain_support.py:32).
